input.question: Why do we have to consciencley swallow a liquid, what is inhibiting it from merely sliding down our throats?
input.ground_truth: Because normally, our airways are open unconsciously, with the epiglottis standing strait up, allowing air to flow in and out. When we swollow, the muscles in our throat push on the epiglottis, closing the larynx, guiding the food to the esophagus and stomach. So, if we were to allow saliva or other fluids to just slide down, without swallowing, it wouldn't be guided into the stomach, it would be guided down our bronchi and lungs, since the airway wouldn't close. Question: Why do we have to consciencley swallow a liquid, what is inhibiting it from merely sliding down our throats?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay, let me explain it like you’re five!

When you drink something, like juice or water, your mouth helps move it to your tummy. But your body wants to make sure the juice goes the right way, not into your nose or out the sides. So, your body has a little helper called your **throat**. 

When you swallow on purpose (that’s what “consciously swallow” means—when you think about it and do it), you close a little door in your throat. This door keeps the juice from going the wrong way and helps it slide safely down into your tummy.

If you just let the juice sit in your mouth and don’t swallow, it can’t get to your tummy because the door isn’t open. That’s why you have to swallow on purpose—to open the door and let the juice slide down safely!

So, your body helps you by making you swallow so the liquid goes where it’s supposed to go.
